review.body:

Tampines Rovers came in with a 33% above average attack and a 3% stingier than average defense (0-0-4, 0.5 scored and 2.5 allowed a game over 4 games), worth about 23 and 23 games of evidence. Projected to score 1.7, they scored 1 (−0.7 goals, 41% under); projected to allow 0.9, they allowed 7 (+6.1 goals, 718% over).

The bigger miss was Shanghai Shenhua's scoring (+6.1 goals against projection).

review.body:
Total: 8 against 2.6 projected (+5.4), about the 99th percentile of the simulated totals (a typical game swings ±1.7).

An outlier: the simulations had a result this far off less than about 5% of the time, which usually means an input was wrong or missing, not just bad luck.

review.body:

The projection missed by a lot, so those flags likely mattered here.

review.title: What the algo learns
review.body:
This game's own lesson: scoring came in at ×2.637 of the raw projection, and the home side beat its projected margin by -6.9 goals. It counts toward Soccer scoring level, home edge and both teams' attack and defense corrections.

Across 1970 graded Soccer games the algo now scales scoring ×0.940 and gives home teams 0 goals. Team corrections so far: Tampines Rovers attack ×0.995, defense ×1.040 (4 games).

review.title: Bottom line
review.body: Wrong side, total outside its normal range, margin outside its normal range (off by 6.8 goals), the pick lost (-1u).
